fields.meta_title: Approval Form That Routes Sign-Offs in Order | Emergent
fields.meta_description: What an approval form should record and how sequential and parallel sign-offs work, plus an app that logs every approver's decision.
fields.h1: Build an Approval Form That Records Every Sign-Off
fields.hero_description: An approval form puts a request in front of everyone who must say yes. Name the approvers and their order, and Emergent builds the form and keeps every decision.
fields.features_heading: Every Approver, in the Order You Set
fields.features_subheading: A printed form ends at a signature line. Emergent's version knows who signs next and which version they signed.
fields.feature_1:
Sequential or parallel chains

Sends each request to approvers one after another, or to several at once when their reviews do not depend on each other. Each step names a specific person or a role you define.
fields.feature_2:
Approval tied to one version

Stores the exact version each approver saw. If the requester edits the document after sign-off, that approval resets and the request returns to the same approver for a fresh look.
fields.feature_3:
Changes requested, with a comment

Gives approvers a third answer besides yes and no. A request for changes goes back to the submitter with the comment attached, then picks up again at the same step once fixed.
fields.feature_4:
Delegates for approvers who are away

Lets each approver name a delegate. A request left unanswered for two business days moves to that person, and the record shows who signed and on whose behalf they signed.
fields.feature_5:
Decisions in Slack or email

Posts each request to the approver as a Slack message or an email with approve and decline buttons, then sends reminders until someone answers or the request escalates.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, your repository

Pushes the full codebase to your GitHub repository. Engineers can add another approval step or a sync to a second system, or ask Emergent to make the change in plain English.

fields.usecase_heading: Approval Chains for Four Kinds of Request
fields.tab_content_1:
An edit after sign-off sends the contract back to legal

Contracts change after legal has read them. Legal approves version 3 of a vendor contract, then the requester changes the payment terms to 45 days. The form sees a new version and resets legal's approval. Legal reviews version 4, and the record keeps both decisions with their dates.
fields.tab_content_2:
Brand, legal and product review it together

Three teams read a launch email, and none of them waits for another. The form sends it to all three at once. Brand and product approve before lunch. Legal asks for a change to the discount wording, and the email goes back to the marketer with that comment. The two approvals stay for the next round.
fields.tab_content_3:
Director on vacation, delegate on record

Vacations stall approvals. A $4,800 laptop order sits with a finance director who is out for the week. After two business days without an answer, the form moves it to the delegate she named before leaving. He approves it, and the record reads: approved by Sam Patel on behalf of Rachel Kim.
fields.tab_content_4:
Student placements approved ahead of any hours

Schools want the placement cleared first. A student proposes 40 hours of service learning at a food bank, and the coordinator approves the site before the first shift. Only hours logged at an approved placement count. Saturday's 6 hours show as 6 of 40, while a shift at a site nobody approved would not count.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Approval Form
fields.howto_description: Most of the work is deciding who signs. The seven steps start with the approvers and end with a record you can hand to an auditor or a dean.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Ask who signs before you design fields. Write down every approver for each type of request. Use roles instead of names where you can, because a role survives a promotion or a resignation. Note which approvals are required and which are advisory.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide whether approvers sign in sequence or in parallel. Sequence suits a chain where each step depends on the last, such as a manager before finance. Parallel suits independent reviews, such as legal and brand reading the same draft.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Collect what the approver will judge: the amount or scope and the reason. Add the date it is needed and any attachment worth reading. Every extra field slows the person submitting and gives an approver one more thing to question.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Let approvers request changes as well as approve or decline, and require a comment whenever the answer is not yes. A decline without a reason tends to come back a week later as a second request with the same problem.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send a reminder when a request has waited two business days, and let each approver name a delegate for absences. Decide in advance what happens when nobody answers. No request should sit in a single inbox for weeks.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Store the file or the field values each approver saw. If anything changes after sign-off, reset that approval. An approval that quietly carries over to an edited document does not cover what the approver read.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Record each decision as data, with the approver's name and a timestamp. Store the version they saw beside it, and export the log when audit or finance asks. A scanned signature on paper shows who signed, but not which draft was in front of them.
